input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects that the accessibility
audit enumerated in the four core Dashboard flows — project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. After this epic, each of the
four flows is fully operable by keyboard alone: focus is never lost or trapped in
modals, no control is unreachable, and visible focus indicators are consistent
across the audited flows. This is the code-level deliverable of the keyboard
accessibility conformance strategy; the updated conformance documentation that
reflects this fixed state is authored separately once this work lands.

## Scope

- Remediate every keyboard-operability defect enumerated in the audit report for
  the four audited flows: focus lost or trapped in modals, controls unreachable
  via keyboard, and tab-order defects.
- Apply consistent visible focus indicators across all interactive controls in the
  audited flows, aligned with the console's design-system focus styling, replacing
  the inconsistent indicator styles the audit identified.
- Cover all four flows end to end: project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, and pipeline run submission, including their modals, forms, and
  multi-step wizards.
- Verify each flow with a scripted keyboard-only walkthrough that exercises every
  audit-enumerated defect.
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require,
  and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end to end using keyboard
  alone, with no focus traps and no unreachable controls, verified by a
  keyboard-only walkthrough per flow in which every audit-enumerated defect passes.
- Every defect listed in the audit report for the four flows is remediated and
  its remediation is verified in the walkthrough.
- Visible focus indicators are consistent across all interactive controls in the
  audited flows, matching the console's design-system focus style.
- Existing automated test suites and the Dashboard build pipeline pass with the
  focus-management changes (no functional regressions).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — the four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls: covered by the modal focus
  management, tab-order, and reachability remediation in this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows: covered by the focus-indicator alignment to the design-system style in
  this epic. HLR-1 and HLR-2 are remediated together because both are satisfied by
  the same pass over the same controls and UI surfaces in the same four flows.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation —
the VPAT and the product documentation accessibility statement — to reflect the
remediated keyboard-accessibility state of the four core Dashboard flows (project
creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission). It is the
published-documentation deliverable required by the public-sector customers before
renewal, and it is authored after the keyboard-accessibility fixes are implemented
so the conformance claims describe the actual shipped behavior.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **VPAT (conformance statement)**: update the keyboard-operability and
  focus-visibility conformance claims for the four audited flows to reflect the
  remediated state, so the published statement matches the fixed product.
- **Product docs accessibility statement**: update the existing accessibility
  statement in the product documentation and republish it to reflect the fixed
  state of the four flows.
- **Technical review**: both documents are technically reviewed against the
  implemented keyboard-accessibility behavior before republication.

Out of scope: documentation of flows or conformance criteria beyond the four
audited flows and the keyboard fixes they received.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT's conformance claims for the four audited flows accurately reflect the
  implemented keyboard-accessibility state: no defect remains claimed as
  conformant, and no conformance claim is made that the implementation does not
  support.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated and republished at
  its canonical location, reflecting the fixed state of the four flows.
- Both documents are technically reviewed against the implementation by
  engineering, and the review sign-off is recorded, before republication.
- The updated VPAT is published at its canonical location.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — the accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review: covered entirely by this epic.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Strategy: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows.

Triage note: the strategy was not triaged as below-threshold or docs-only. Although
the scope is small, it spans two architecturally distinct work streams that warrant
separate PR review cycles — Dashboard code remediation (keyboard operability and
focus indicators) and substantive conformance-documentation authoring (VPAT and
accessibility statement, new/rewritten published content). Per the Step 0 escape
conditions, both streams were decomposed in full.

The strategy reports no open questions ("the audit report enumerates the exact
defects per flow"), so no Investigation epics were created. The Dashboard is
Konflux-onboarded (per architecture context), so no onboarding-chain epics are
needed.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 — Dashboard keyboard accessibility fixes (P1)"] --> E002["E002 — VPAT / accessibility statement update and republish (P2)"]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementation epics) | The conformance documentation describes the fixed state; the VPAT claims and the accessibility statement can only be written and technically reviewed against the implemented keyboard-accessibility behavior. E001 is the only other Implementation epic, so it is the sole blocker. |

No other edges: E001 has no dependencies (the audit enumerates the defects; the
Dashboard repo and build pipeline already exist), and there is exactly one
implementation work stream in the Dashboard component, so nothing runs in parallel
with anything else.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | E001 | Keyboard operability of the four audited flows. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | E001 | Consistent visible focus indicators. Covered in the same epic as HLR-1: both HLRs are remediated by the same pass over the same controls and UI surfaces in the same four flows — focus traps, reachability, and focus indication are one keyboard-accessibility change per control, so splitting them would build/audit the same surface twice. Same priority (P1), so no priority split is involved. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | E002 | VPAT and product-docs accessibility statement update, republish, technical review. |

All three HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections (non-blocking).** The strategy has no Impacted Teams
   table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
   Non-Functional Requirements section. Decomposition proceeded with available
   information. Team assignments were derived: the Dashboard epic's team
   (RHOAI Dashboard) comes from
   `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`; the
   Documentation epic's team (RHOAI Documentation) is inferred — verify with the
   strategy author before scheduling.
2. **Epic size over the ~2-week guideline (managed).** E001 is estimated at
   ~1 sprint (the audit enumerates the exact defects per flow; remediation is
   mechanical focus-trap/reachability/indicator work across four flows in one
   codebase). Kept whole because the four flows are one logical change owned by one
   team in one repo, and a per-flow split fragments a single mechanical remediation
   pass while duplicating the shared focus-management and focus-indicator baseline
   across epics. Re-split trigger: the audit defect list for any single flow
   exceeds ~10 defects, or total remediation tracking passes the 2-week guideline —
   at that point split per flow, with each flow epic still carrying the shared
   focus-indicator consistency requirement.
3. **Possible priority inversion (non-blocking).** HLR-3 is P2, yet the problem
   statement says two public-sector customers require the published VPAT before
   renewal — a commercially gating deliverable. Per the docs-authoring priority
   exception the epic is P2 (strategy frontmatter priority: Normal), but scheduling
   should account for the renewal deadline; the fix work (E001) is correctly P1 and
   is on the critical path to the VPAT regardless.
4. **Component mapping note.** "Documentation" has no architecture-context file but
